speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic, I am Dr. Agent. To help me understand the cause of your acute diarrhea, please describe exactly what your symptoms are, when they started, and if you have had any recent travel or changes in your diet. Also, have you noticed any fever or blood in your stool?

speaker: Patient
text: 58-year-old female. The patient has been treated for community-acquired pneumonia with levofloxacin on the medical floor. She reports developing watery diarrhea with at least 9 episodes within the last two days, accompanied by lower abdominal discomfort and cramping.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Clostridioides difficile infection.

This patient is an elderly female who recently received levofloxacin for pneumonia, a major risk factor, and now presents with frequent watery diarrhea and cramping. Given the high clinical probability, I am proceeding to confirm the diagnosis with a stool assay.

REQUEST TEST: C. diff Toxin A/B Stool Assay
